Sam (support): Hey team, customer on prod reported intermittent 502s hitting /v1/generate. They supplied a request_id: `req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c`. Can someone check server logs + retention? :eyes:
Ana (sre): Copy — can you paste the full req_id exactly as they sent it and the approximate client timestamp (they're in PST)?
Sam (support): Full id above, client says ~2026-03-16 18:12:04 PST. Also they attached a curl repro: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
Raj (infra): On retention — prod logs are hot for 30 days, then roll to cold for 365 days read-only. But quick heads-up: our KQL index uses UTC timestamps, so we'll need to convert their PST time. PST is UTC-8 (or -7 with DST).
Liz (eng): I'll try a Kibana search. Use this KQL to find the request_id across index-*:
```
request_id: "req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c" OR message: "8f3b9c"
```
Sam (support): Ran that and only saw a few edge logs, nothing obvious. Any special queries for gateways or edge-runtime?
Ana (sre): Try narrowing to upstream and gateway logs: `service.name: (gateway OR edge-runtime) AND request_id: "req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c"` — if not found, expand to `*8f3b9c*` because some systems truncate/prefix.
Liz (eng): Also check the router trace for `trace_id` mapping, sometimes request_id is in `http.request_id` field. Example KQL: `http.request_id: "req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c" OR fields.request_id: "req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c"`
Raj (infra): If Kibana returns nothing, the log may have aged into cold-storage index `archive-*`. Use the timeframe 2026-03-16T23:00:00Z..2026-03-17T00:00:00Z to cover their local 18:12 PST.
Sam (support): Customer also reported latency spikes right before 502; asked if we can run a quick tail on the host. Any host mapping from request_id?
Ana (sre): If we find the router entry, look for `upstream.host` or `host.hostname` in the same event. If you want me to look I can run `log-sleuth --id req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c --backfill 30m` (internal tool) and dump the matching hostnames. :thumbsup:
Liz (eng): I dropped a sample command for reproducing logging locally (for devs):
```
# reproduce with request-id header
curl -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_KEY" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c" \n  -d '{"input":"trigger 502"}' \n  https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
Sam (support): Customer willing to provide a debug bundle. Asking what we need in it.
Raj (infra): We need: request_id, client IP, full response headers, approximate client time, and the curl -v output. Also ask them to run a tcpdump if they can (optional). For internal handoff, attach the debug bundle and the outcome of `kubectl logs` from the host once we identify it.
Ana (sre): I'll run log-sleuth now — pinging svc account: `@DebugBot start-sleuth req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c window=30m`
DebugBot: sleuth job started (job id sleuth-8892). Searching indices: logs-prod-*, archive-2026-03. Estimated results: 12 events.
Ana (sre): Found router and upstream errors around 2026-03-17T02:12:06Z. Gateway returned 502 with upstream_code=504 from model-host-17. I'm pulling the host logs now.
Liz (eng): If upstream returned 504, could be model timeout. Check model queue depth and tokenization errors.
Sam (support): Noted. I'll update the customer: request_id found, logs show gateway 502 proxied from model-host-17 with upstream 504. Asking if they can run the curl repro with `-H 'X-Request-Id: req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c'` and attach the full verbose output + timestamp.
Customer-Bot: Thanks — running repro now, will attach verbose output and client timestamp in PST.
Raj (infra): Final note for handoff: since their local time is PST, convert to UTC for searches or use Kibana quick range `@timestamp >= "2026-03-17 02:00:00" AND @timestamp <= "2026-03-17 02:30:00"` (UTC). Also if we need to pull from cold storage file a request: `archive-export --id req_2026-03-17_8f3b9c --format json` and that will take ~20m.
Sam (support): Thanks everyone. I'll collect the debug bundle and repro and follow up in this thread once customer attaches. :handshake:
